subject: Partial session resets impacting hosted inference — status update
body:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Morales <ben@storix.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial session resets impacting hosted inference — status update

Hi Ben / Elena,

I'm reaching out with an update and next steps — we observed a spike in session reset errors affecting a subset of streaming and long-lived chat sessions starting ~08:45 PT today. We've opened an incident on our status page (link below) and are actively triaging.

What we saw:
- Intermittent 502/connection-closed responses for tokens streamed after ~6k tokens in active sessions.
- Error rates concentrated in our us-west-1 pool; small percentage of customers saw elevated retry/backpressure.
- No evidence of data loss; requests that fully retried succeeded in most cases.

Immediate impact for Storix Labs (from initial telemetry):
- ~2% of API requests from your account experienced session resets between 08:45–09:05 PT.
- You may have seen partial completions or truncated streams in a small fraction of calls.

Actions underway (engineering):
- We’ve activated a targeted reroute for your tokens to an alternate capacity pool to reduce session stickiness.
- Rolling an incremental fix that adjusts the KV-cache eviction threshold (will deploy to canary in the next 30m).
- Capturing a full timeline (attached) and asked infra to surface connection-level logs.

What we need from you:
- If you have high-priority requests that experienced truncation, please reply with 2–3 sample request IDs and shorttimes (we’ve requested logs but customer-supplied IDs speed correlation).

We’ll send a follow-up with ETA for resolution and a brief post-incident summary when we have the full timeline. Apologies for the disruption — we know reliability is fundamental.

Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: incident-timeline-20250522.csv (text/csv), reference: storix-sample-logs-05-22.txt (text)

body_3:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Morales <ben@storix.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 10:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial session resets impacting hosted inference — status update

Ben — thanks for the IDs, that helped. Quick technical summary for the thread:

Root cause hypothesis (ongoing):
- A sudden metadata churn in the KV-index layer caused nondeterministic eviction behavior under a narrow workload profile (long-lived sessions + high prefix cache pressure).
- The eviction window caused some KV lookups to miss mid-stream and triggered our connection abort safety path.

Immediate mitigations we applied (10:00–10:04 PT):
- Incremental eviction threshold increase rolled to Canary hosts in us-west-1.
- Demand-driven reroute enabled for Storix tokens; this pins your sessions to a pool with higher KV headroom.
- Throttled batch prefetch for long sessions to reduce transient pressure.

Expected impact:
- Error rate should drop to baseline within 15–25 minutes post-deploy; slight P95 latency increase (~10–20ms) possible due to reroute. No cost changes expected from the reroute itself — it's a capacity reallocation within your current tier.

Next steps / ETA:
- Monitoring window for 30 minutes; will post a confirmatory update at ~10:35 PT.
- Post-incident writeup and recommended SDK best-practices for long-lived sessions will be shared within 72 hours.

Aditya / Evelyn: I’m pinning you for the postmortem ownership and SDK guidance draft.

Sean
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
